notes: This is a typescript sheet with handwritten additions and typewriter cancellations. It continues a prior sentence at sent, then discusses the direct-image functor and begins section 3.1.3.

The upper addition says u-star commutes with familiar functorial constructions expressible in terms of inductive limits and finite projective limits, with examples involving free objects and tensor products. These are the sheet’s assertions, not results independently proved here.

The main paragraph says direct image preserves algebraic structures defined only by projective limits, but generally fails right exactness and even preservation of epimorphisms. It links that defect to cohomological properties studied in the following exposition. Its added bottom note lists comodule, bialgebra and torsor structures and free-module/tensor-product constructions.

Section 3.1.3 asks for all exactness properties and possible adjoints of a functor between U-toposes to be made explicit in order to understand its geometric nature. It conditionally identifies a colimit-preserving and finite-limit-preserving f with u-star, for u in the reversed direction, and ends in a statement about a left adjoint.

The words “s’il s’avère que” introduce a condition. I found no explicit “not proved” or similar mathematical hesitation on this sheet. The unsettled readings in this report are palaeographical, not source statements of doubt.
The sheet bears pen page number 23, an inverted archive number 39 at upper left, and section 2 corrected to 3 in 3.1.3. No date, title sheet or total page count is present.
The source refers to § 6 plus bas, the preceding footnote, and the following exposition. None of those external passages was consulted.

H begins with an explicit editorial synopsis and only directly quotes selected marginal additions. Its paraphrases were not treated as direct assertions about whether local typed words are live or cancelled. The actual source omissions are recorded separately.
The thin marks below De plus and above the bottom continuation bound additions. No semantic alphabet value is assigned to either pair of loop-and-stem call signs.
